purpose: Preserve a portable system model of MAK's archive-to-learning circulation without promoting hypotheses, products, or scores into authorial truth.

included: external opportunity constraints and explicit fit bindings
curatorial, portfolio, application, and research compilation
bounded outcome learning and plan-only autonomy
excluded: authorship, intention, or artistic identity inference
truth promotion from scores, filenames, drafts, or model outputs
scope.case_policy: ARICA, MYRA, RAYU, ISKVW, and Fondart are evidence-bearing cases, never architectural types.

authorities.rule: Files and native artifacts remain authoritative for their bytes and observable structure; observation is read-only.
/home/mak/flujo defines executable contracts but does not replace physical source authority.
/home/mak/WIN is not an active runtime and is not proof of integration.
Opportunity documents can establish requirements and validity only within their own source scope.
A verified external receipt can evidence an outcome episode, not the truth of artistic claims.

evidence_summary.readiness_claim: No universal archive readiness is claimed. Portability remains a falsifiable objective requiring cross-archive conformance and independent outcome groups.

gaps: Project and work identity across renamed or moved snapshots lacks a generally validated cross-archive identity protocol.
Public manifestation joins remain sparse and cannot be inferred from local exports.
Technical witness receipts need a generic practice-evidence adapter with semantic scope controls.
Official opportunity validity needs bounded refresh and triangulation.
Portability has not been demonstrated on independent artist archives with held-out evaluation.
Outcome learning lacks enough independent identity groups for policy promotion.
